Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 31-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  Operating Systems [IT_3128]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                      Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Apply your understanding of multiprogramming and timesharing to explain how CPU utilization and        (4)  
  system responsiveness differ between the two.  
  A)           Construct an example scenario where timesharing provides a clear performance advantage over  
  multiprogramming.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Apply your understanding of process states and schedulers to explain how a process transitions         (4)  
  among different states.  
  Develop a scenario where multiple processes share the CPU, and illustrate how different  
  schedulers coordinate to maintain efficient CPU utilization.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)           The following C code snippet is given:                                                                 (2)  
  #include < stdio.h>  
  #include < unistd.h>  
  
  int main() {  
  $$pid_t pid = fork();$$  
  $$if (pid == 0)$$  
  printf("Child process endsn");  
  else {  
  printf("Parent runningn");  
  sleep(10);  
  }  
  return 0;  
  }  
  Identify the state of the child process after termination and before the parent process exits.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                Four processes arrive at time 0 with the following burst times:                                        (4)  
  $$P1 = 5 ms, P2 = 10 ms, P3 = 15 ms, P4 = 20 ms.$$  
  A)           Assume the time quantum for Round Robin is 5 ms, and context switch time is negligible.  
  Compare the average waiting time for these processes under Preemptive SJF and Round Robin  
  scheduling.  
  Analyze which algorithm gives a better trade-off between CPU utilization and response time,  
  providing a short justification.  
  
  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)   Two processes P0 and P1 are implementing Peterson's solution.                                           (4)  
  At some point, the variables hold the following values:  
  $$turn = 0;$$  
  $$flag[0] = true;$$  
  $$flag[1] = true;$$  
  and both processes are in their while (flag[j] && turn == j) loop.  
  Construct a sequence of events to show which process will enter the critical section first, and justify  
  why the three critical-section requirements are or are not violated under this interleaving.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   Compare the function of binary and counting semaphores in terms of the number of resources              (2)  
  managed and their effect on process synchronization.  
  Provide one example scenario where using a counting semaphore is essential over a binary  
  semaphore.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
3)                                                                                                                (4)  
  
  
  A)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)   A system uses the Banker's Algorithm for resource allocation. Process P1 currently holds some          (4)  
  resources and makes a new request for additional resources. The operating system must check  
  whether granting this request keeps the system in a safe state.  
  Construct the sequence of logical steps the operating system should follow to solve this problem  
  using the Banker's safety algorithm.  
  Explain how the system can utilize the "pretend allocation" step to identify if the new request should  
  be granted or deferred.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)                                                                                                           (2)  
  
  
  Page #2

Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)        A system has a memory of 300 KB divided into the following free blocks (holes):                     (4)  
  $$Hole 1 = 70 KB, Hole 2 = 120 KB, Hole 3 = 40 KB, and Hole 4 = 60 KB.$$  
  A)   Four processes arrive sequentially with memory requirements:  
  $$P1 = 50 KB, P2 = 80 KB, P3 = 30 KB, P4 = 60 KB.$$  
  Apply Best-Fit and Worst-Fit algorithms to allocate memory to these processes.  
  Show the allocation table and final memory state after all allocations.  
  Finally, identify which strategy results in less total external fragmentation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)   A computer system uses base and limit registers for memory protection and relocation.               (4)  
  
  The base register of a process contains the value 40,000.  
  The limit register contains the value 12,000.  
  A user process generates the following logical addresses: 10,500, 14,500, and 12,200.  
  
  Develop the address translation scheme for this system and determine which of the above  
  addresses will cause a trap to the operating system.  
  Further, explain how the MMU (Memory Management Unit) utilizes these registers during context  
  switching to ensure memory protection.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   Two processes, P₁ and P₂, share the same physical memory space using a global page                  (2)  
  replacement algorithm.  
  During execution, you observe that P₁'s page faults increase dramatically whenever P₂ starts  
  execution.  
  Contrast the behavior of global and local page replacement strategies in this scenario.  
  Justify with proper reasons which approach would better control thrashing.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)        A process with 4 page frames executes the reference string:                                         (4)  
  0, 1, 2, 3, 2, 1, 4, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.  
  A)   All frames are initially empty.  
  Contrast the number of page faults obtained using the FIFO and Second-Chance (Clock)  
  algorithms.  
  Show the intermediate state of the reference bit (use binary notation), and conclude whether  
  Second-Chance successfully reduces unnecessary replacements.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)   A disk has 200 cylinders (0-199). The disk arm is currently at cylinder 100, moving toward the  (4)  
  higher-numbered cylinders.  
  Pending I/O requests are for cylinders:  
  176, 79, 34, 60, 92, 11, 114, 139, 150.  
  Construct the sequence of servicing requests using both SCAN and C-SCAN scheduling  
  algorithms.  
  Compute the total head movement in each case and identify which algorithm provides more uniform  
  waiting time.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   Apply your understanding of file access methods to identify which method would be most efficient    (2)  
  for:  
  a) A compiler accessing variable symbol tables.  
  b) A media player reading large continuous audio files.  
  Briefly justify your choice in each case.  
  
  Page #3

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
